title: Das zweyte Silentium Dei (pseudo-Johann Arndt), cipher passages, Glücksbrunn 1798 (Beinecke Mellon MS 136; DECODE R2873)

steps.what: Found the book on Yale Digital Collections (OID 10187248) through the browser (the site blocks curl); read the manifest and downloaded all 69 images from the IIIF server.
Contact sheets of all openings; located cipher on pp. 24-76 (one full page, 30 short passages inside clear sentences) and a key figure on p. 83.
Read the p. 83 figure: pigpen-type grid with dotted second letters, triangle cells t/u, v/w, y, z, and a ligature table; tested on the start of p. 24 (zeigen, deren) and p. 29.
Web search found Schmeh's 2022 Cipherbrain post (p. 24 plaintext from Lasry and Kopal; key on p. 83 noted) and Rieber's comment with most short passages.

Read all 31 passages sign by sign at full resolution with the p. 83 key; p. 24 checked against the published plaintext (agrees, three corrections); short passages checked against Rieber (four passages new, several misreadings corrected).
Re-read doubtful words at 2x crops (p. 75 sta=cken, p. 54 gutter word); p. 24 letters A-S checked against the apparatus plates on pp. 21-23.

Transcribed the clear German around every cipher passage (pp. 24-32, 43-48, 50-56, 59-63, 69-71, 73-77) with two image-reading agents and translated the 13 recipes that carry cipher into English; the clear text shows the p. 60 cipher "Glas No. S." should be P.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcription.txt and reading.txt linked, with the clear-text translations clear/pp24-49.md and clear/pp50-77.md; the 2022 p. 24 reading (Lasry's transcription, Kopal's decryption) and Rieber's blog comment are listed separately as pointers to Schmeh's post, since neither text is in the repository.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): reading.txt (all 31 passages) reads; Rieber's 2022 comment, a pointer with partial entries, and the 2022 p. 24 pointer (nothing of either in the repository) left out of outcome.texts; reading_review A on the project's reading. Claim unchanged.

outcome.method_basis: The book carries its own key (p. 83, 'Die Figur unserer geheimen Schrift'), applied unchanged to all 31 passages; the p. 24 passage had been read in 2022 (Lasry transcription, Kopal decryption, on Schmeh's blog) and most short passages by a blog commenter, found after the key was read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription.txt via decode.py: 1,545 cipher signs, 2 unread ({?})
outcome.notes: Key drawn in the book, used unchanged. p. 24 was already read online (2022); this is the first complete, gap-checked reading of all passages. Not a letter: an alchemical manuscript book (pseudo-Arndt, Rosicrucian-Paracelsian) describing a burning-glass 'magische Machine'. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the two pointers to Schmeh's Cipherbrain post (the 2022 p. 24 reading by Lasry and Kopal, and Christof Rieber's comment of 10 March 2022, a partial list with entries cut short) are left out of outcome.texts: nothing of either text is in the repository, and Rieber's list does not read as sentences (per-document C). Both are credited in NOTES and on the page.

texts.summary: A 129-page alchemical manuscript book, Das zweyte Silentium Dei (pseudo-Arndt, copied at Glücksbrunn in 1798), describing a 'magische Machine' of three burning glasses that focus sunlight onto glass dishes and capels. The cipher words are the working parts of the recipes: vessels and materials, procedures, and on p. 24 the key to the lettered figures of the machine.

reading_review.note: reading.txt gives every cipher passage in its clear sentence; the p. 24 block reads as a continuous German description of the machine ("No. A. B. C. zeigen die hohlgeschliffene Glaesern ..."), with one {?} and two [C] doubtful words; the short passages are words and phrases that complete their clear sentences. Translated in clear/pp24-49.md and pp50-77.md. The per-document C concerned Rieber's 2022 blog comment, not this reading.
